Metadata.title: Trading Academy
Metadata.description: A free academy for learning crypto trading — from your first candlestick chart to advanced strategies.

Footer.disclaimer: Educational content only – not financial advice.

hero.badge: Free · English and Czech · no Lambo on the front page
hero.title: Learn to trade crypto – before the market teaches you
hero.description: The market teaches too, it just charges a lot per lesson. Here it is free: clear lessons from your first candle to your own trading plan, real charts, quizzes – and no “guaranteed signals”.

why.title: Why here
why.description: Because the internet has more “gurus” than a chart has candles. We are the boring friend who first asks how much you can afford to lose.

free.title: Free. Really.
free.description: No paywall, no “VIP channel” and no 399-euro course that teaches you to buy a 799-euro course.

structured.title: Step by step
structured.description: Course → module → lesson. You always know where you are and what comes next – unlike the price of Bitcoin.

levels.title: From zero to your own plan
levels.description: Start from the very beginning, or jump in where you are. Every course has a clear level: beginner, intermediate, advanced.

risk.title: Risk comes first
risk.description: We talk about losses before profits. Not because we are pessimists – but because losses will come. The point is to keep them small.

levels.title: Pick your level
levels.description: Whether you have never seen a candlestick chart or you have already burned your fingers once.

beginner.name: Beginner
beginner.description: Crypto is new to you and you want to know what you are getting into.
topics: What a blockchain is and why cryptocurrencies exist at all
Exchanges, wallets and how not to get your account stolen

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.description: You know the basics and want to trade by a plan, not by mood.
topics: Indicators, order types and real costs
Position size, a trading plan and a journal

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: You trade and want to do it better – or find out it is better to stop.
topics: Managing the risk of a whole portfolio

curriculum.title: Courses
curriculum.description: Short lessons, real charts and a quiz at the end of every module. Bring your own coffee.

free.question: Is it really free?
free.answer: Yes. You do not have to enter a card, an e-mail or the name of your first pet. All courses are free and will stay free.

rich.question: Will it make me rich?
rich.answer: Honestly? Probably not. Most people who trade lose money in the long run. We teach you to understand the market, manage risk and decide deliberately – and to recognise when it is better not to trade at all.

advice.question: Is this financial advice?
advice.answer: No. Trading Academy is educational content. We explain how markets work and how to manage risk – we never tell you what to buy or sell.

money.question: Do I need money to start learning?
money.answer: No. You can learn everything without spending a cent. When you do decide to trade, only use money you can afford to lose – not your rent.

courses.question: Which courses are available?
courses.answer: You will find all finished courses in the Courses section above and on the Courses page. More – including advanced ones – are in the works.

languages.question: Which languages are available?
languages.answer: English and Czech. You can switch the language any time in the header – the lesson stays the same, it just speaks differently.

chart.illustrative: Illustrative data, not a real market
chart.logarithmic: Logarithmic axis: equal distance = equal percentage change

legend.bollinger: Bollinger Bands 20, 2 (the middle line is SMA 20)
legend.vwap: VWAP 14 – volume-weighted average price over the last 14 candles
legend.sar: Parabolic SAR 0.02 / 0.2 – green dots below the price, red above it
legend.supertrend: Supertrend 10, 3 – green below the price, red above it
legend.rsi: RSI 14 (panel below the chart, lines at 30 and 70)
legend.atr: ATR 14 – average range as % of price (panel below the chart)
legend.macd: MACD 12, 26, 9 (panel below the chart: MACD in blue, signal in yellow, histogram)
legend.stochRsi: StochRSI 14, 14, 3, 3 (panel below the chart: %K in blue, %D in yellow, lines at 20 and 80)
legend.stochastic: Stochastic 14, 1, 3 (panel below the chart: %K in blue, %D in yellow, lines at 20 and 80)
legend.kdj: KDJ 9, 3, 3 (panel below the chart: K in blue, D in yellow, J in purple, lines at 20 and 80)
legend.williamsR: Williams %R 14 (panel below the chart, lines at −20 and −80)
legend.cci: CCI 20 (panel below the chart, lines at +100 and −100)
legend.obv: OBV – cumulative volume (panel below the chart)
legend.mfi: MFI 14 (panel below the chart, lines at 20 and 80)

doji.name: Doji
doji.description: Open and close are almost the same – buyers and sellers are in balance and the market hesitates.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.description: After a fall, sellers pushed the price down, but buyers pushed it back up – a possible turn upwards.

shootingStar.name: Shooting star
shootingStar.description: After a rise, buyers pushed the price up, but sellers pushed it back down – a possible turn downwards.

bullishEngulfing.name: Bullish engulfing
bullishEngulfing.description: A green body completely covers the previous red one – buyers are taking over.

bearishEngulfing.name: Bearish engulfing
bearishEngulfing.description: A red body completely covers the previous green one – sellers are taking over.

morningStar.name: Morning star
morningStar.description: A big red candle, a small hesitant one and a big green one – a turn from a fall to a rise.

eveningStar.name: Evening star
eveningStar.description: A big green candle, a small hesitant one and a big red one – a turn from a rise to a fall.

anatomy.label: Parts of a candlestick: a rising and a falling candle. The body is between the open and close price, the wicks reach the highest and the lowest price.

blockchain.caption: Every block stores the fingerprint (hash) of the previous one. Changing an old block would change its hash and break every block after it.

sign.title: Sign
sign.text: The sender signs the payment with their private key in the wallet.

broadcast.title: Broadcast
broadcast.text: The wallet sends the transaction to the network, computers pass it on to each other.

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.text: Miners or validators check it and write it into a new block.

receive.title: Receive
receive.text: The receiver sees the coins once the block is added – more blocks on top mean more certainty.

transaction.caption: No bank sits in the middle – the network itself checks and records every payment.

privateKey.title: Private key
privateKey.text: The secret that controls your coins. Never share it with anyone.

publicKey.title: Public key
publicKey.text: Calculated from the private key. Proves your signature.

address.title: Address
address.text: Short form of the public key. Share it to receive payments.

wallet.caption: Each step works only forward: from an address nobody can find your private key.

orderBook.label: Illustrative BTC/USDT order book
orderBook.caption: Sellers wait above the price, buyers below it. The bars show how much is waiting at each price. Illustrative data.

sharedLedger.caption: Four notebooks agree, one does not. The village trusts the majority – George's twenty chickens stay a dream.

midnightEdit.label: Cartoon: at night, George secretly writes 20 chickens into his notebook by candlelight, while a chicken at the window stares in disbelief.
midnightEdit.caption: George quietly "improves" his notebook at night. The chickens have their doubts.

copyMachine.label: Cartoon: a cheerful person presses the button of a copy machine that spits out banknotes.
copyMachine.caption: If money could be copied like a file, everyone would be a millionaire. At least until lunch.

miningRace.label: Cartoon: three sweating computers race to guess a number while an electricity meter spins wildly.
miningRace.caption: Mining in a nutshell: millions of guesses per second – and an electricity meter that never rests.

pizzaDay.label: Cartoon: a happy person with two pepperoni pizzas and a price tag of 10,000 BTC.
pizzaDay.caption: 22 May 2010: two pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins, then about 41 dollars. Probably the most expensive dinner in history.

vendingMachine.label: Cartoon: a surprised customer at a vending machine labelled 'if coin → snack' that hands out a snack without any shop assistant.
vendingMachine.caption: Smart contract in a nutshell: the rules are written in code and run on their own – nobody can bend them. Not even when you ask nicely.

memeSlot.label: Cartoon: a Shiba Inu pulls the lever of a slot machine labelled MEMECOIN; the reels show ×100, ×100 and −99%.
memeSlot.caption: Memecoins in a nutshell: two reels promise a hundredfold, the third one is usually right.

feeBus.label: Cartoon: a full bus leaving in 10 minutes; a passenger waving banknotes gets on, a person with one coin waits at the stop.
feeBus.caption: Fees as a bus ride: whoever offers more gets a seat first. The rest wait for the next bus.

marketShout.label: Cartoon: a buyer shouts 'Buying at 64,990!', a seller shouts 'Selling at 65,010!', and the exchange between them drops a coin into its fee jar.
marketShout.caption: An exchange is a market where buyers and sellers never quite agree – and the exchange earns a little either way.

shadyBooth.label: Cartoon: a shady booth with a flashing '1000 % A YEAR!' sign and a salesman in sunglasses next to a boring booth with a licence certificate.
shadyBooth.caption: Choosing an exchange: the boring booth with a licence beats the flashing promises.

stickyNote.label: Cartoon: a seed phrase written on a sticky note on a monitor, and a thief with binoculars at the window.
stickyNote.caption: Where not to keep your seed phrase: anywhere someone else can see it.

firstBuy.label: Cartoon: a slightly nervous person in front of a big green Buy button, with a checklist being ticked off.
firstBuy.bubble: I'll check the address… a third time.
firstBuy.caption: The first purchase: small amount, checklist, deep breath.

phishingHook.label: Cartoon: a hooded hacker fishes with an email marked with an exclamation mark, a worried user reaches for it.
phishingHook.caption: Phishing: the bait is always urgent. The more urgent, the more suspicious.

giveawayScam.label: Cartoon: a fake celebrity on a screen with sparkles promising 'Send 1 BTC → get 2 back!', a viewer gets excited.
giveawayScam.caption: Nobody gives away free money on the internet. Especially not twice as much as you send.

receiptPile.label: Cartoon: a person at a desk with a calculator, surrounded by flying receipts.
receiptPile.caption: Tax season without records: a lot of paper and even more questions.

tortoiseHare.label: Cartoon: a calm tortoise labelled INVESTOR and a sweating hare with a phone labelled DAY TRADER racing to a finish flag.
tortoiseHare.caption: The tortoise and the hare, crypto edition. The hare is still checking his phone.

candleSurfer.label: Cartoon: a surfer riding on top of a wave made of rising candlesticks.
candleSurfer.caption: Riding a trend is fun – until the wave ends. And it always ends.

parachuteStop.label: Cartoon: one jumper floats down calmly under a parachute labelled STOP-LOSS, another falls without one towards '−100 %'.
parachuteStop.caption: A stop-loss is a parachute: you open it before the ground gets close.

graduation.label: Cartoon: a graduate with a cap and a diploma under falling confetti.
graduation.caption: The end of the course – and the start of careful, patient learning.

stairsDown.label: A shopper with a SALE bag walks happily down a staircase whose every step is lower than the last
stairsDown.caption: Every step down is a lower high and a lower low. It is not a sale until the stairs turn around.

ceilingFloor.label: A ball bounces on the slab between two floors while a surprised person downstairs looks up
ceilingFloor.caption: Role reversal: what stopped the price from below can hold it up from above.

zoomLenses.label: Two boards: a smooth rising line labelled week and a nervous zigzag labelled hour under a magnifying glass, and a worried person
zoomLenses.bubble: From afar calm, up close panic.
zoomLenses.caption: The same market on two timeframes. Look at the big picture before the magnifying glass.

dogWalk.label: A dog labelled price zigzags on a leash while its owner labelled average walks calmly
dogWalk.bubble: Easy, we will get there together.
dogWalk.caption: The price runs back and forth, the moving average walks calmly behind it – it never runs ahead.

speedometer.label: A speedometer with the needle deep in the red zone above 70, showing RSI 85
speedometer.caption: A high RSI says the move is fast. It does not say the brakes are coming.

crowdRoar.label: A packed stand of fans cheering together labelled big volume and one lonely fan labelled small volume
crowdRoar.caption: A move many people join counts for more than one lonely shout.

crystalBall.label: A fortune teller in a pointed hat looks into a flickering crystal ball with chart lines
crystalBall.caption: Indicators are calculated from the past. The crystal ball only shows what has already happened.

orderRemote.label: A tall remote control with buttons market, limit, stop and OCO, one of them being pressed, and a worried person
orderRemote.caption: Know what each button does before you press it with real money.

feeTermites.label: Three little bugs labelled fee, spread and slippage nibble at a wallet full of coins
feeTermites.caption: Costs are small bugs. You will not notice one – a hundred take a big bite out of the wallet.

jengaLeverage.label: A wobbly tower of blocks with 100× on top and a person holding one more block
jengaLeverage.caption: Every extra multiple of leverage is another block on a tower that is already swaying.

cakeSlice.label: A whole cake cut into many slices labelled account, and one small slice on its own plate labelled 1R
cakeSlice.caption: The account is the cake, one trade is one small slice. Losing a slice is fine – losing the cake is not.

coinFlip.label: A spinning coin between two signs: win plus 2R with 40 percent and loss minus 1R with 60 percent
coinFlip.bubble: I count the average, not one flip.
coinFlip.caption: You lose more often than you win – and on average it can still come out positive. Or not: it all depends on the numbers.

pilotChecklist.label: A pilot in a cap ticks a checklist on a clipboard, next to him a trader who keeps the plan in his head
pilotChecklist.bubble: I have the plan in my head!
pilotChecklist.caption: Pilots use a checklist after ten thousand hours of flying. Traders after ten trades think they do not need one.

detectiveDiary.label: A detective in a hat examines an open trading journal with a magnifying glass
detectiveDiary.bubble: Why did I buy that on Tuesday?
detectiveDiary.caption: The journal remembers what you would rather forget – and that is exactly why it is useful.

fomoTrain.label: A sweaty trader runs with an outstretched arm after a green train labelled to the moon that is already leaving the station
fomoTrain.caption: FOMO makes you run after a train that has already left. The next one always comes – the station is called a plan.

happyNews.label: A smiling person reads a newspaper headline saying Bitcoin to a million, while a paper saying Bitcoin falls lands in a bin
happyNews.headline: BTC TO $1M!
happyNews.caption: Confirmation bias: the good news gets read twice, the bad news goes straight to the bin.

hammockRest.label: A trader rests in a hammock between two trees, a closed laptop lies on the grass
hammockRest.caption: No position is also a position. Sometimes the best trade of the week happens in a hammock.

chartCoaster.label: A rollercoaster cart rides on tracks shaped like a chart, the passenger with arms up wears a seatbelt labelled plan
chartCoaster.bubble: With a seatbelt it is fun!
chartCoaster.caption: Crypto can be a rollercoaster. The courses are about how to fasten your seatbelt.

guruMegaphone.label: An internet guru in sunglasses and a gold chain shouts promises through a megaphone, next to him someone calmly reads the first lesson about risk
guruMegaphone.caption: On the left a promise, on the right an education. Guess which one wants to sell you something.

regimeWeather.label: A weather presenter points at a forecast of four market regimes: calm and wild trend, calm and wild range with a lightning bolt
regimeWeather.caption: Before you go out, check the weather. Before you open a trade, check the market regime.

followTheLeader.label: A big duck labelled BTC leads, the ducklings ETH, SOL and MEME follow
followTheLeader.caption: Altcoins mostly go where Bitcoin goes. And when it stumbles, they fall even harder.

cycleAstrologer.label: An astrologer in a starry hat points at three dots labelled 2016, 2020 and 2024 joined by a line
cycleAstrologer.bubble: Three dots = a law of nature!
cycleAstrologer.caption: Three cycles look like a pattern. A statistician would say they are three dots.

feverThermometer.label: A big thermometer labelled funding shows a high fever, next to it the market lies under a blanket
feverThermometer.caption: High funding is the market's temperature. It does not say when the fever breaks – only that the patient is overheated.

recipeChef.label: A recipe with exact steps and a nice cake next to a burnt, smoking cake made by a cook who cooks by eye
recipeChef.step4: 4. Take out, even if it smells good
recipeChef.bubble: I just do it by eye.
recipeChef.caption: With a recipe you can find out why the cake failed. By eye, only that it failed.

strategyToolbox.label: A toolbox with three tools – trend, mean reversion and breakout – and a person holding a hammer who does not know what to use it on
strategyToolbox.bubble: Can't I drive screws with a hammer?
strategyToolbox.caption: Each type of strategy is a different tool. A trend hammer will not help in a range.

breathingStop.label: On the left a big boat on a calm sea, on the right a small boat in a storm with lightning
breathingStop.bubble: In big waves, a smaller boat.
breathingStop.caption: Volatility-based sizing: a bigger boat in calm water, a smaller one in a storm – the risk stays the same.

timeTraveler.label: A trader steps out of a time machine holding tomorrow's newspaper with the headline BTC plus ten percent
timeTraveler.headline: BTC +10%
timeTraveler.caption: Look-ahead: a test that knows tomorrow's price always wins. You will not know it.

dashboardPilot.label: A pilot in a cockpit with four gauges – return, drawdown, trades, costs – holding a hand over three of them
dashboardPilot.bubble: One gauge is enough for me.
dashboardPilot.caption: Watching only the return is flying without an altimeter. Metrics are always read together.

examCheat.label: A surprised student facing a new exam while last year's answers fly away
examCheat.bubble: I have never seen these questions!
examCheat.caption: A strategy that learned past data by heart fails the exam it has never seen.

testPilot.label: A small plane with a test pilot wearing a parachute flies among clouds, the plane labelled demo
testPilot.caption: A new plane flies without passengers first. A new strategy trades without money first.

eggsBasket.label: A figure trips over a banana peel and three eggs labelled BTC, ETH and SOL fall out of a basket – all of them break
eggsBasket.bubble: But I spread it over three eggs!
eggsBasket.caption: Three correlated positions are one basket. One peel breaks them all at once.

kellyGauge.label: A speedometer of risk per trade with green, yellow and red zones; the needle shakes in the red zone beyond the Kelly number and the engine smokes
kellyGauge.caption: Up to the Kelly number, more risk speeds up growth. Beyond it, only smoke.

drawdownStairs.label: A figure with a backpack of risk walks down the stairs of a drawdown past signs: half the risk at 10%, a quarter at 20%, stop at the bottom
drawdownStairs.bubble: The lower I go, the lighter the pack.
drawdownStairs.caption: Drawdown rules are written in advance – on the way down the stairs, thinking gets hard.

reportCard.label: A happy trader holds their own report card: an A for following the rules, a C for profit
reportCard.title: REPORT CARD
reportCard.caption: The monthly review grades mainly you. The profit of a single month is largely luck.

crowdedPond.label: A pond full of fishing rods, the last fish swims away, a worried angler stands next to a sign saying They bit here
crowdedPond.caption: When everyone finds the good spot, the fish run out. A strategy's edge fades the same way.

hammockTrader.label: A trader sleeps in a hammock between trees, a phone with a price alert lies on the grass
hammockTrader.caption: The alert watches the market while you rest. Trading for years, not weeks.

speedRace.label: A race car labelled SOL speeds along the top lane, below it a snail labelled a block every 10 minutes crawls
speedRace.bubble: A block in a fraction of a second!
speedRace.caption: Solana bets on speed. It pays for it with powerful hardware and fewer validators.

metronomeChoir.label: A metronome keeps time and three singers sing; the middle one wears a solo badge because the schedule says it is their turn
metronomeChoir.caption: The leader schedule is known in advance, and Proof of History keeps them in a shared rhythm.

pitStop.label: A race car stands in the pit smoking, next to a restart sign; a worried mechanic calls the others
pitStop.caption: After an outage the network does not restart by itself – validators have to agree on a joint restart.

bathtubSupply.label: A bathtub filling from an inflation tap and emptying through a burn drain; a SOL rubber duck bobs on the water
bathtubSupply.caption: Inflation adds new SOL faster than fee burning removes it. But the tap is slowly closing.

tokenMailboxes.label: A wall of mailboxes labelled SOL, USDC and JUP; a new MEME mailbox lands with a tag saying 0.002 SOL deposit
tokenMailboxes.bubble: A new mailbox? That is a deposit.
tokenMailboxes.caption: Every token has its own account in your wallet. Close an empty account and the deposit comes back.

tollBooth.label: A toll booth marked priority: one car drives through the fast lane, three cars wait in a queue
tollBooth.caption: A priority fee buys a place in the queue, not a better price.

twoKeys.label: A big token and two keys on a hook labelled mint and freeze
twoKeys.bubble: I will keep the keys, just in case.
twoKeys.caption: Whoever holds the keys to the printer and the freezer decides more about your tokens than you do.

blankCheque.label: A smiling stranger hands over a paper titled airdrop to sign; the small print says send everything
blankCheque.title: AIRDROP
blankCheque.bubble: Just sign here, it is a gift!
blankCheque.caption: A drainer does not steal a password. It gets you to sign a transaction that takes everything.

stakeCalendar.label: A piggy bank next to a calendar with pages epoch 1, 2 and 3; coins drop into the piggy bank
stakeCalendar.caption: Staking rewards arrive with every epoch – and unstaking follows the same rhythm.

coatCheck.label: A theatre cloakroom: a coat labelled SOL hangs on a rail and a figure holds a ticket labelled staking token
coatCheck.bubble: I can even sell the ticket!
coatCheck.caption: Liquid staking gives you a ticket for your SOL. Just note that in a panic it sells at a discount.

shoppingRobot.label: A robot with a shopping cart moves between three stalls priced 151, 150 and 152
shoppingRobot.caption: An aggregator checks every pool and splits the trade for the best price. It does not check whether a token is genuine.

rocketFactory.label: A row of six rockets: five only wobble, one green one jumps; above them a sign saying one in a hundred
rocketFactory.bubble: This one will fly, for sure!
rocketFactory.caption: Only about one in a hundred new memecoins makes it further. And even that one may not fly.

tokenDetective.label: A detective in a hat with a magnifying glass goes through a checklist: mint, freeze, holders, liquidity
tokenDetective.caption: Ten minutes with a block explorer exposes most traps. It does not turn a token into a good investment.

rollercoaster.label: A rollercoaster with signs 260, 8, 296 and 60 at its peaks and troughs; a cart with riders at the top
rollercoaster.caption: The real peaks and troughs of SOL. The ride goes on – and nobody knows where.

dogOnLeash.label: A figure labelled BTC walks a dog labelled SOL that runs back and forth on its leash
dogOnLeash.caption: SOL sometimes runs ahead and sometimes lags – but mostly goes where Bitcoin goes.

solanaSummit.label: A hiker with a backpack stands on a mountain top with a Solana flag, confetti falling around
solanaSummit.caption: You have finished the course. Take the ten rules with you.

hotelSafe.label: A hotel safe labelled your crypto and, behind the reception desk, a smiling receptionist with a spare key dangling from a finger
hotelSafe.bubble: I have the key, do not worry.
hotelSafe.caption: On an exchange, the exchange holds the keys. Convenient – as long as it is honest and stays open.

masterKey.label: A big golden key labelled seed and three doors labelled BTC, ETH and SOL opening
masterKey.caption: A seed phrase creates the keys to all your accounts. Whoever has it has everything.

walletPockets.label: A phone labelled pocket, a safe labelled savings and a paper flying off in the wind
walletPockets.bubble: Phone for coffee, safe for savings.
walletPockets.caption: A hot wallet for small change, a hardware wallet for savings – and paper only as a backup.

trustTheScreen.label: A laptop shows a different address from the hardware wallet's screen; the laptop address is crossed out
trustTheScreen.caption: An infected computer can lie. The hardware wallet's screen shows what you are really signing.

sealedBox.label: A card with a pre-filled seed phrase peeks out of a parcel and a surprised figure raises a hand to stop
sealedBox.caption: Only your device creates the seed phrase. A pre-filled card means someone else knows it.

addressCompare.label: Two almost identical addresses one above the other; a magnifying glass shows they differ in the middle
addressCompare.caption: A poisoned address matches at the start and at the end. It differs where nobody looks.

fireTest.label: A campfire burns a paper backup, next to it lies an undamaged steel plate
fireTest.caption: Stainless steel survives a fire, paper does not. A second copy elsewhere survives even a whole house burning.

secretDoor.label: A bookshelf with a secret door opening onto a safe; a happy figure stands next to it
secretDoor.bubble: No password, just the living room.
secretDoor.caption: A passphrase opens a completely different wallet. Whoever finds the seed phrase finds only the living room.

twoOfThree.label: A chest with two keyholes and three keys numbered 1, 2 and 3; keys 1 and 2 drop towards the chest
twoOfThree.caption: A split backup: one share reveals nothing, two recover the money.

letterForFamily.label: A figure at a desk writes a letter titled for the family
letterForFamily.title: FOR THE FAMILY
letterForFamily.bubble: What, where and whom to call.
letterForFamily.caption: The letter says where to find the backups – not what is in them.

phishingHookWallet.label: An email saying verify your seed phrase hangs on a fishing hook and a worried figure watches it
phishingHookWallet.caption: No honest party asks for your seed phrase. Not the manufacturer, not the exchange, not support.

securityShield.label: A blue shield with a tick, confetti falling around and a happy figure next to it
securityShield.caption: One afternoon of work and a few years of peace. And a check once a year.

licenseCheck.label: Professor Wick checks two exchange buildings: one has a MiCA licence stamp, the other a closed for the EU stamp
licenseCheck.caption: Neither size nor a famous name replaces a licence. Check it in the regulators' registers.

idSelfie.label: A figure holds an ID card and a phone with a selfie frame
idSelfie.bubble: A neutral face? I cannot do that.
idSelfie.caption: An ID and a selfie are normal at sign-up. A request for your seed phrase never is.

securityToggles.label: Security settings with five switches turned on and Professor Wick next to them
securityToggles.caption: Five switches turn your account from a tent into a fortress.

depositPipes.label: A wide SEPA pipe with coins flowing and a narrow card pipe with a toll booth
depositPipes.caption: A euro transfer is often free; a card takes a percentage.

screenTour.label: A simplified exchange screen with numbered parts: trading pair, chart, order book, recent trades, order panel and your orders
screenTour.caption: Six parts almost every exchange has: 1 pair, 2 chart, 3 order book, 4 recent trades, 5 order panel, 6 your orders.

quickBuyMarkup.label: Two shops with the same coin: a shiny quick buy with a higher price and a plain spot stall with a lower one
quickBuyMarkup.caption: Quick buy hides a markup in the price. Spot shows the fee openly.

orderForm.label: An order panel with Price, Amount and Total fields and Professor Wick next to it
orderForm.caption: Price × amount = total. Read the summary before confirming.

makerTaker.label: A counter with coins: on the left a maker putting goods out, on the right a taker taking them; fees above them
makerTaker.bubble: Whoever stocks the shelf pays less.
makerTaker.caption: A maker adds an offer to the book, a taker takes it. The exchange rewards those who fill the market.

timeframeZoom.label: Two charts side by side: a jittery minute chart and a calm daily one
timeframeZoom.caption: A shorter timeframe shows more noise. Start longer; shorter is only for timing.

indicatorSoup.label: A candle chart buried under five coloured indicator lines and a fallen Professor Wick next to it
indicatorSoup.bubble: This is no longer a chart, it is soup.
indicatorSoup.caption: More lines do not mean more certainty. Volume, an average and RSI are enough to start.

alarmLine.label: A chart with a horizontal level line and a ringing alarm clock
alarmLine.bubble: It rings when there is something to do.
alarmLine.caption: A price alert watches the chart for you. It buys nothing, it just lets you know.

depthMountains.label: A depth chart as two mountains, green on the left and red on the right, with Professor Wick standing in the spread gap between them
depthMountains.bubble: Down here in the valley is the spread.
depthMountains.caption: Steep mountains mean many offers near the price. The valley between them is the spread.

dangerButtons.label: Four big colourful buttons for futures, bonus, copy trading and Earn, with Professor Wick next to them
dangerButtons.bubble: I am not touching these yet.
dangerButtons.caption: The shiniest buttons lead to leverage, fees and risk. If you do not know what they do, leave them alone.

withdrawJourney.label: Professor Wick carries a coin from the exchange building to a home safe
withdrawJourney.caption: The right network, the whole address, a small test amount – and the coins are home.

candleRecipe.label: Professor Wick throws candles into a pot and a smooth blue line comes out
candleRecipe.caption: Every indicator is a recipe: it takes candles, does a calculation and gives a line. Nothing more, nothing less.

threeFamilies.label: Three doors labelled trend, oscillator and volume
threeFamilies.caption: Almost every indicator in the menu belongs to one of three families.

periodKnob.label: A big period knob with the values 7, 25 and 99 and Professor Wick next to it
periodKnob.caption: The period is the most important setting: it decides how many candles the indicator takes into account.

slidingWindow.label: A dashed frame slides over the candles; every candle in it weighs 1×
slidingWindow.caption: SMA is a window that slides along the chart. Inside it, every candle is equally important.

averageRace.label: Three lines, EMA, WMA and SMA, race after the price; EMA is the closest
averageRace.caption: The more weight new candles get, the sooner the average reacts – and the more often it is wrong.

bollingerTube.label: Purple bands around the candles are narrow when calm and wide in a wild market
bollingerTube.caption: Bollinger Bands inflate and deflate with how wildly the price moves.

vwapBalance.label: A balance: five small coins on one pan, one big BTC coin on the other outweighs them
vwapBalance.caption: VWAP computes the average price so that big trades have more say than small ones.

sarHop.label: Green dots below rising candles, then they jump above the falling candles as red ones
sarHop.caption: Parabolic SAR chases the price with dots. When the price overtakes them, the dots jump to the other side.

supertrendRail.label: A green stair-step handrail under rising candles and a happy Professor Wick above it
supertrendRail.caption: In a rise, Supertrend only moves up. It jumps down only when the price really turns.

rsiThermometer.label: An RSI thermometer reads above 70 and Professor Wick sweats next to it
rsiThermometer.caption: RSI above 70 means the market is running up fast. It does not mean it has to fall right away.

doubleEspresso.label: A wildly swinging line between 20 and 80 and two coffee cups labelled RSI
doubleEspresso.caption: Stochastic RSI is the RSI of RSI – more sensitive, faster and very restless.

rangeElevator.label: A lift in a shaft between a green high and a red low; the car labelled close is near the high
rangeElevator.caption: Stochastic and KDJ ask: on which floor between the low and the high did the price close?

upsideDown.label: Professor Wick hangs upside down from the ceiling next to a scale from 0 at the top to −100 at the bottom
upsideDown.caption: Williams %R is the stochastic turned upside down: 0 at the high, −100 at the low.

rubberBand.label: A rubber band stretched from the blue dashed average line up to a point at +180
rubberBand.caption: CCI measures how far the price is from its average – in multiples of the usual deviation.

twoTrains.label: A fast blue train overtakes a slow yellow one; green bars of the gap grow below them
twoTrains.caption: MACD watches two trains – a fast and a slow EMA – and measures the gap between them.

volumeCrowd.label: Rising candles with green volume bars below that grow fast towards the end
volumeCrowd.caption: Volume shows how many people joined a move. A rise with a crowd behind it is stronger.

piggyBank.label: A piggy bank: three plus coins fall in, one minus coin falls out
piggyBank.caption: OBV is a piggy bank: it adds the volume of up days and subtracts the volume of down days.

moneyPipes.label: An MFI box with a green pipe where money flows in and a red one where it flows out
moneyPipes.caption: MFI is like RSI, but it counts money: price times volume.

cleanDesk.label: A clean chart with one average and one oscillator; MACD, KDJ, CCI and WR labels pushed aside
cleanDesk.caption: A clean setup: one trend indicator, one oscillator, volume. Everything else goes.

divergenceArrows.label: The green price arrow climbs while the red indicator arrow below it falls; Professor Wick is puzzled
divergenceArrows.caption: Divergence: the price makes new highs, but the indicator does not. A warning, not an order.

tugOfWar.label: Two indicators play tug of war with Professor Wick in the middle
tugOfWar.caption: Indicators often disagree. Then your plan decides – not the one that says what you want to hear.

legend.sma: SMA {period} (blue). Highlighted candles = the ones the current value is computed from.
legend.ema: EMA {period} (yellow). Highlighted candles = the ones the current value is computed from.
legend.bollinger: Bollinger Bands {period}, 2: the dashed middle line is SMA {period}; the upper and lower bands lie two standard deviations from it.
legend.rsi: RSI {period} in the panel below the chart, lines at 70 and 30. Highlighted candles = the price change being counted.
legend.macd: Over the candles EMA 12 (blue) and EMA 26 (yellow). In the panel MACD (blue), the signal line (yellow) and the histogram.
legend.stochastic: Stochastic %K {period} in the panel, lines at 80 and 20. Dashed: the high (green) and low (red) of the highlighted candles.
legend.atr: ATR {period} in the panel below the chart – in USDT, not in percent.
legend.obv: OBV in the panel below the chart: a running total of volume.

explain.sma: add up the closes of the last {period} candles – {sum} in total. Divide by {period} and SMA = {value}.
explain.emaFirst: EMA has to start somewhere. Its first value is a plain average of the first {period} closes: {value}.
explain.ema: EMA moves {weight} of the way to the new price: {previous} + {weight} × ({close} − {previous}) = {value}.
explain.bollinger: the average of the last {period} prices is {middle}, and prices typically deviate from it by {deviation}. Upper band = {middle} + 2 × {deviation} = {upper}, lower = {lower}.
explain.rsiFirst: the first RSI. Over the last {period} candles the average rise was {gain} and the average fall {loss}. The ratio is {strength}, so RSI = 100 − 100 / (1 + {strength}) = {value}.
explain.rsi: the price changed by {change}. The average rise and fall move 1/{period} of the way towards that change: rise {gain}, fall {loss}. The ratio is {strength}, so RSI = {value}.
explain.macd: fast EMA 12 = {fast}, slow EMA 26 = {slow}. MACD is their difference: {macd}. The signal line (EMA 9 of MACD) = {signal}, the histogram bar = MACD − signal = {histogram}.
explain.stochastic: over the last {period} candles the high was {high} and the low {low}. The close {close} sits at {value}% of that range – (close − low) / (high − low) × 100.
explain.atrFirst: the first ATR is a plain average of the true ranges of the last {period} candles: {value}.
explain.atr: the true range is the largest of: high − low ({range}), the jump up from yesterday's close ({upGap}) and the jump down ({downGap}) – so {trueRange}. ATR = ({previous} × {periodMinusOne} + {trueRange}) / {period} = {value}.
explain.obvUp: the candle closed higher ({close} vs {previousClose}), so its volume is added: {previous} + {volume} = {value}.
explain.obvDown: the candle closed lower ({close} vs {previousClose}), so its volume is subtracted: {previous} − {volume} = {value}.
explain.obvFlat: the candle closed at the same price as the one before, so OBV does not change: {value}.

indicatorPeriod.outside: The price broke out of the bands {count}×.
indicatorPeriod.zones: The line entered the overbought or oversold zone {count}×.
indicatorPeriod.tempoFaster: A shorter period: the line reacts faster and gives more signals – false ones included.
indicatorPeriod.tempoSlower: A longer period: the line is calmer with fewer false signals, but it reacts late.
indicatorPeriod.tempoStandard: Binance's default setting – try moving the slider both ways.

chartQuiz.pick: Pick a candle – click the chart or use the slider (arrow keys work too).
chartQuiz.candle: Picked candle {date}: open {open}, high {high}, low {low}, close {close}.
chartQuiz.answerRange: The right candles are from {from} to {to} (green).

orderSimulator.intro: A practice BTC/EUR market – no exchange, no real money. Try the orders from the lesson and the mistakes that cost the most.
orderSimulator.marketPrice: Price: the best offers in the book (market order)

refused.notEnoughQuote: You do not have enough euros for this purchase (the fee counts too).
refused.notEnoughBase: You do not have that much bitcoin.
refused.stopWouldTrigger: The stop is exactly at the last price – the order would trigger at once and the exchange rejects it. Put the stop above or below the current price.

summary.fills: You {side, select, buy {buy} other {sell}} {amount} BTC at an average price of {average} – across {levels, plural, one {# price level} other {# price levels}} of the book. Taker fee {fee}.
summary.rests: {amount} BTC {side, select, buy {to buy} other {to sell}} at {price} will wait in the book. When it fills, you pay the maker fee of {fee}%.
summary.stop: When the price {direction, select, up {rises} other {falls}} to {stop}, a limit order to {side, select, buy {buy} other {sell}} {amount} BTC at {price} is created.
summary.jumpFills: Even if the price jumped past the stop to {jump}, the limit would still fill.
summary.jumpMisses: Careful: if the price jumped past the stop straight to {jump}, the limit would not fill and you would stay in the trade.

warning.farFromPrice: The price is {percent}% {direction, select, below {below} other {above}} the last price. Is a zero missing, or one too many?
warning.crossesSpread: The limit is past the best offer on the other side, so the order executes now – at the book's prices, not at yours – and you pay the taker fee.
warning.wholeBalance: This order bets your whole balance.
warning.noRoom: The stop and the limit are the same. In a sharp move the limit then easily fails to fill – leave some room between them.
warning.bookExhausted: There are not enough offers in the book – only part will fill.
warning.oppositeStop: {side, select, sell {The stop is above the current price, so the sale triggers only on a rise – it takes profit, but does not protect you from a fall.} other {The stop is below the current price, so the purchase triggers only on a fall – “I will buy when it drops”.}}

orderSimulator.openStop: Stop {stop} → {side, select, buy {buy} other {sell}} {amount} BTC at {price}
